answer: We formalize Sybil resistance by bounding each identity to a dynamic opportunity-cost bond combined with a subgame-perfect slashing matrix triggering under zero-knowledge delay audits. When malicious nodes attempt to split identities, expected payoffs scatter through a prism of penalties, forcing the utility function to remain strictly negative. Under these constraints, any strategy allowing an agent to wander from honest validation generates a deficit, like a broken sonnet failing its rules, ensuring a stable Nash equilibrium.
